REFUTED the escalated N-3 claim that `make check-all` in a lane worktree is a fail-open merge gate (alleged: exits 0 having run no lint and no tests). No upstream request filed to agentic-protocol-monorepo, because the defect does not exist in this tree. Evidence, three independent points: 1. The fail-open `exit 0` on "No test commands configured" lives in `mk/lane-worker.mk:38-41`, which is DEAD CODE. Root `Makefile` includes `mk/lane-worker.mk` at line 147 and `-include Makefile.d/*.mk` at line 976; root `Makefile.d/` exists and ships `lane-gate.mk`. GNU make confirms the override verbatim: `Makefile.d/lane-gate.mk:239: warning: overriding commands for target 'lane-check'` / `mk/lane-worker.mk:8: warning: ignoring old commands`. 2. The winning definition is deliberately fail-closed on this exact case. `Makefile.d/lane-gate.mk:30-37` documents the status contract: `LANE_GATE_STATUS=skipped` exits 2, `passed` exits 0, and "Skipped and passed do not share a representation." A lane declaring no verification therefore exits 2, not 0. 3. `check-all` (`Makefile:362-386`) runs under `set -eu`, so a `$(MAKE) lane-check` exit 2 aborts the recipe before the success banner prints. Separately measured: in the FEBT-2 worktree `IN_ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT=0`, `LANE=` (empty), so `IN_LANE_WORKTREE=0` (`Makefile:67`) and `make check-all` there takes the else branch and runs the full monorepo suite. The lane-scoped branch is not reachable from task-start worktrees at all. Also resolved while here: the 2 rg-016 PHP `class_exists` failures were stale-classmap only. `php -r "require 'vendor/autoload.php'; class_exists('AltContext\\Api\\Services\\PersonResolutionService')"` now returns true; `composer.json` declares both psr-4 and `classmap: ["src/"]`, and `vendor/` is gitignored so a clean `composer install` regenerates it. Measured on the VM (claude 2.1.287, bwrap 0.9.0), contradicting the docs [DATA-17]. (1) With no filesystem settings, sandboxed Bash can write all of /home, /tmp and /var/tmp, and credential dirs are readable. (2) The sandbox leaves empty mount-placeholder files in HOME and cwd after the run (.bash_profile, .bashrc, .profile, .gitconfig, .npmrc in HOME; .env*, package.json, yarn.lock, node_modules and others in cwd). An empty ~/.bash_profile stops the login shell sourcing ~/.profile, which logged VM claude out; fixed by deleting only the placeholders from that run. (3) denyWrite beats allowWrite and cwd. (4) What does confine: absolute denyRead, network.allowedDomains [], CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 (forces default mode), HOME redirected, cwd under /var/tmp, and denyWrite of /home, /tmp and the out dir. Residual: /var/tmp stays writable. Rules: never run it with the real HOME; with claude -p in an ssh heredoc add < /dev/null; stage explicit paths only.

Three lessons from DESCPICK-3 remote author/review staging: 1. A canon overlay staged with `rsync -aL` from heuristics-canon-current keeps the copy's read-only mode bits. A two-file planning slice (assessment + README index) needs two per-subject pass review runs and two serialized plan-accept runs.
